root_motivation: Grounding (mcphost-1 /healthz read 2026-10-05 2:55pm PDT): claim_email_configured: false, tenants_claimed: {external: 0, synthetic: 0} against signups.external: 14 and paying_tenants: 0; src/email.rs:21-25 reads MCPHOST_EMAIL_API_URL/API_KEY/FROM and :62 said 'Resend or Postmark is still undecided at build time'; journey.py:62 listed claim in NON_P0_STEPS, so the daily journey passed 12/12 with the claim path unexercised; the market-test vision's weakest link (leaf 5, 'the human will open a claim link, verify an email, and pay -- assumed') had had no data since the claim PRD shipped 09-24. Fourteen strangers had signed up and zero were claimable: the agent is told (skill.md step 5) to relay a link that leads to a page that cannot send the email. The one assumption the whole market test exists to measure had no sensor.
user_persona: Four (PRD User stories): an agent on its first successful publish, told once to hand its human the claim link; a human who opens it, enters an email, clicks the magic link, and sees what their agent built; the operator (Joe), whose deploy probe must go red on prod until mail env is set and whose healthz must show claimed tenants per week; the daily journey, which must exercise the claim page for real against the test mail client and fail the run if it breaks.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given an implicit first call, a /u/new mint, a URL-bound first call, and an invite join, When each response's onboarding envelope is read, Then it carries claim_url, and host.whoami carries the same URL until the tenant is claimed.

Given an unclaimed external tenant's first successful host.tool_publish, When the response is read, Then _meta.next.kind = "claim" with the URL; given its second publish, Then no claim nudge is present; given a synthetic tenant, Then never.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/ownmt_ac02_claim_nudge_on_first_publish.rs -- three tests, using mcphost::control::signup(..., "8.8.8.8", ...) directly to force origin: "external" (the harness's own default tenants are loopback/synthetic and would never qualify); exercises the real wire-level _meta object, not structuredContent's next field (see hard_constraints).

acceptance_criteria.description: Given MCPHOST_EMAIL_PROVIDER = postmark and a fake API, When a claim email is issued, Then the request matches Postmark's shape; given resend (default), Then Resend's; given a 500 from the API, Then the claim call returns claim_email_failed with a request_id and the journal row carries the status code and no key.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/ownmt_ac03_email_provider_shape_and_failure_journal.rs -- three tests built on a server_with_provider(mock, provider) helper that points a real HttpEmailClient at a wiremock::MockServer, asserting the outbound request/header shape per provider and the journal row's status code (and absence of the key) on a simulated 500.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given three external claims and one synthetic claim in the window, When /healthz is read, Then claims.external = 3, claims.synthetic = 1, and median_minutes_to_claim is computed from owner_verified_at - created_unix.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/ownmt_ac04_healthz_claims_block.rs -- one test using a claimed_tenant() helper that signs up then back-dates via db::set_claim_timing_for_test to control the 30-day window deterministically.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a host whose env contract requires mail and claim_email_configured = false, When mcphost-deploy probe runs, Then the artifact check fails with claim-email-unconfigured and doctor names the missing variables; given the variables set, Then the check passes.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/ownmt_ac05_claim_email_configured_signal.rs -- pins the mcphost-side claim_email_configured healthz field that mcphost-deploy's probe reads. The probe/doctor/env-contract behavior itself was already fully implemented in ~/repos/mcphost-deploy by a prior commit (41a8398, env_contract.py/probe.py/cli.py/artifact.py, with its own test_mail_env_ac1/ac2/ac3 files) before this dispatch began; this test closes the local gate-ready criterion without duplicating that work.

acceptance_criteria.test: tests/ownmt_ac06_claim_round_trip_for_journey_claim_step.rs -- pins the one contract the journey step actually depends on: signup's claim_url, POST /claim/{token} (form email), the magic-link token extractable from the fake mail client's captured message by the exact /claim/verify/([A-Za-z0-9_-]+) pattern the journey step's own extractor uses, GET /claim/verify/{code}, and host.whoami.owner_verified flipping true. The journey harness itself (synthorg's journey.py claim step, promoted from an always-skip P1 stub to this real round trip) and mcphost-deploy's rollback wiring (claim leaving NON_P0_STEPS; journey.py reading payload["claim"] directly) are real commits in ~/repos/synthorg (cc0d1e6, branch wm-build/mcphost-ownership-moment-journey-claim-p0) and ~/repos/mcphost-deploy (fbf6892, same branch name), not this repo -- see hard_constraints for the ordering bug found and fixed there.

additional.ac6_claim_step_ordering_bug_found_and_fi: The first implementation of synthorg's _claim_result called it from run_journey AFTER _run_once returned -- by then the journey's own teardown step had already called host.self_offboard, removing the tenant from the fixture/live host, so host.whoami's owner_verified check spuriously read as unclaimed even when claim_verify itself had succeeded. five_whys_trace.q: Why do agents still perform the retired key-flow ritual and why can nobody claim a tenant?
five_whys_trace.a: The claim path needs an outbound email and no provider is configured on prod; the open question ('Resend or Postmark', market-test vision, owner Joe) was never closed before the original claim PRD shipped on 09-24, so it shipped provider-agnostic.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did an unconfigured mail provider reach prod at all?
five_whys_trace.a: Nothing in mcphost-deploy's probe fails when claim_email_configured is false -- a missing env var produces a silently-passing deploy, not a red one.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did nothing flag the gap for ten days after it shipped?
five_whys_trace.a: The readiness list treated claim as a feature that had already shipped; journey.py marked claim a NON_P0_STEPS member (line 62), so the daily journey passed 12/12 with the claim step unexercised the entire time.

five_whys_trace.q: Why was claim allowed to sit in NON_P0_STEPS instead of gating the journey like every other customer-facing step?
five_whys_trace.a: synthorg's own journey.py reported claim as a separate top-level key, never a steps list entry, so its NON_P0_STEPS membership in mcphost-deploy's journey.py was already dead code -- nobody had noticed the set entry did nothing, which is a different, deeper bug than merely 'claim should be P0'.

five_whys_trace.q: Why was the ownership moment allowed to be optional at every one of these levels?
five_whys_trace.a: The product's persona is the agent (profile thesis); the human was added as the payer late, and nothing after the claim page was built to pull the human in -- the agent is told once (skill.md step 5) to relay a link that cannot be delivered, and nothing downstream of that single mention ever checks that it was. Deepest actionable level: the human's entry was documented as the agent's job and instrumented as nobody's.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the claim nudge ride structuredContent.next (PRD-mcphost-one-next-tool's existing hint channel) or the real wire-level MCP _meta object the requirement's own text names?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The real _meta object (meta.0.insert("next", ...)). structuredContent.next is already asserted by nexttool_ac04 to carry exactly {tool, why} for a young tenant's early calls; a second, claim-shaped entry there would break that pinned test. The harness's own default test tenants are loopback/synthetic and would never qualify for an external-only claim nudge regardless, but the _meta channel was chosen on architectural grounds (literal match to the requirement's own wording) independent of that fact.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Was requirement 5 (mcphost-deploy probe fails claim-email-unconfigured) still open work for this dispatch?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- git history in ~/repos/mcphost-deploy showed it already landed at commit 41a8398 before this dispatch began, with its own env_contract.py/probe.py/cli.py/artifact.py changes and test_mail_env_ac1/ac2/ac3 tests. This dispatch added only a thin mcphost-side pinning test (AC5) rather than re-implementing or duplicating that commit.

ambiguities_resolved.question: For requirement 6 (journey claim step promoted to P0), was removing "claim" from mcphost-deploy's NON_P0_STEPS set sufficient on its own?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- that set was never actually consulted for claim (synthorg reports claim as a top-level key, not a steps list entry), so removing the dead set entry alone would not have changed rollback behavior at all. The real fix was making journey.py's _evaluate_steps read payload["claim"] directly and fail when its verdict is "fail".
